How Does SCRIPE Enforce Enterprise Security Assurance & Platform Hardening Across All 19 Modules?

Long image

A

Answer

SCRIPE enforces 5-layer zero-trust defense across 19 backend modules, Next.js 16, and the CLI/CI toolchain. All 48 JSENTINEL findings and 26 net-new platform threats are remediated and verified by 391 automated security tests.

  1. JSENTINEL 48/48 Reconciled: 13 confirmed live-drift and app-hardened findings closed, 31 verified bundle AST false positives documented, and 4 managed-edge informational items bounded.
  2. 26 Net-New Threats & 7 Review Catches Closed: 3 Critical (TH-API-01 webhook HMAC, TH-TEN-01 DSR ownership, TH-TEN-02 custom-domain DNS TXT), 15 High, and 8 Medium findings remediated alongside 7 independent review fixes.
  3. 5-Layer Defense & Nonce CSP: Per-request 128-bit x-nonce CSP, 6-pass CSS/SVG sanitization, postMessage origin-plus-source validation, and DNS-pinned SSRF handlers protect all boundaries.
  4. 4-Layer Proof & Cutover Boundary: 318 xUnit, 65 Vitest, 8 live Chromium E2E journeys, and 100/100 security arch-check rules gate code release and external production cutover.

Applies toSCRIPE-Backend (49b8f5c76) + SCRIPE-Frontend (d8ec386ad) + SCRIPE-CLI (268f169) + Root (d1c5fdb)

How Do the 5 Defense Layers, Nonce CSP, Tenant Isolation & DNS-Pinned SSRF Connect?

Diagram structure
  • Next.js Nonce Proxy edge_csp
  • Sanitizer & sw.js v3 client_store
  • Kestrel & FallbackPolicy api_ingress
  • 19-Mod Tenant & DSR Guard tenant_fls
  • DNS-Pin SSRF & HMAC ssrf_crypto
  • CLI Arch-Check & 0-CVE ci_audit
  • edge_csp → client_store · x-nonce + Origin
  • edge_csp → api_ingress · HTTPS + CSRF
  • api_ingress → tenant_fls · 4x9 PBAC + FLS
  • tenant_fls → ssrf_crypto · Outbox + FixedTime
  • ci_audit → api_ingress · BE/FE Rules + RE2

Click any highlighted node below to inspect how Next.js per-request nonce CSP, client storage guards, Kestrel ingress policies, 19-module tenant/DSR/FLS guards, DNS-pinned SSRF handlers, and CI supply-chain gates interlock.

  1. Per-Request Nonce CSP & Frame Policy ↗

    src/proxy.ts and security-headers.ts mint a 128-bit cryptographic x-nonce per request, enforce script-src 'self' 'nonce-<b64>', and restrict SAMEORIGIN framing strictly to /en/dashboard/studio/preview/* (DENY elsewhere).

  2. Sanitization, postMessage & sw.js v3 ↗

    6-pass sanitize-css.ts strips url()/@import/Unicode escapes, sanitize-svg.ts blocks dangerous tags, postmessage-security.ts verifies origin+source+schema, /sw.js (scripe-v3-static-only) excludes /api/ & /auth/, and logout wipes storage.

  3. Kestrel Ingress, FallbackPolicy & no-store ↗

    Global FallbackPolicy (TH-TEN-05) closes anonymous mutation fallbacks, RateLimitingMiddleware fails closed in production (TH-TEN-06), ForwardLimit = 2 hardens proxy trust (E1), and GET/POST login emit Cache-Control: no-store.

  4. 19-Module Tenant, DSR, FLS & Custom Domain ↗

    CreateDataSubjectRequestCommandHandler enforces SubjectUserId == callerUserId (TH-TEN-01), AddCustomDomainCommandHandler requires _scripe-verify.<domain> DNS TXT (TH-TEN-02), and FieldMaskingHelper / RequireOperationalScope protect all 19 modules.

  5. DNS-Pinned SSRF & Constant-Time Webhooks ↗

    SsrfSafeHttpClientHandlerFactory pins validated public IPs in ConnectCallback with AllowAutoRedirect = false (TH-API-02, B2-1), Paymob/PayPal/Elsystem webhooks enforce constant-time HMAC (TH-API-01, TH-API-03), and plugin JWTs use an isolated secret (TH-API-04).

  6. Static Security Rules, Fail-Closed Audit & RE2 ↗

    BE-040..042 and FE-034..036 enforce domain-first naming and security rules (100/100), scripe audit --json fails closed on advisories (01fa10b), .gitleaks.toml uses Go RE2 syntax (d1c5fdb), and Dockerfile runs rootless (cc11ad9e5).

How Does the 4×9 Domain-Identity Assurance Flow Execute & What Governs External Production Cutover?

Every request is evaluated across 4 domain tiers (D1 Central Auth, D2 Tenant Subdomains, D3 Custom Domains, D4 Invalid/SQLi). It simultaneously enforces 9 identity tiers (I1 Protected Super Admin through I9 Suspended Accounts and Tenants).

Diagram structure
  • Browser / Playwright browser
  • Next.js Nonce Proxy proxy
  • Studio Preview Guard studio
  • .NET 10 API Ingress api
  • Tenant, DSR & SSRF Guard guard
  • browser → proxy · GET /en/auth/signin or /en/dashboard/studio
  • proxy → browser · x-nonce CSP + DENY (or SAMEORIGIN on /preview/*)
  • browser → studio · Dispatch cross-origin postMessage spoofing payload
  • studio → browser · Reject mismatched event.origin / event.source / schema
  • browser → api · Anonymous or cross-tenant POST / DSR / Webhook
  • api → guard · FallbackPolicy + SubjectUserId + FixedTimeEquals
  • guard → api · 401/403/400 + tenant-prefixed cache key
  • api → browser · Fail-closed response + Cache-Control: no-store

Release Readiness Verdict: Scoped GO vs. Conditional NO-GO for External Production Cutover

Code, pre-production, and local UAT hold a Scoped GO (a64aa9a4f Backend, d8ec386ad Frontend, 268f169 Dev-Tools, d1c5fdb root). Unconditional external production cutover remains a Conditional NO-GO until four live infrastructure gates pass. Gate 1 requires Vercel production redeploy (>= d8ec386ad) serving per-request x-nonce CSP and scripe-v3-static-only /sw.js. Gate 2 requires Railway production deploy (>= efc0c6219) with ForwardedHeaders__ForwardLimit=2, ForwardedHeaders__KnownNetworks__0, and GeoIp__OriginVerificationSecret. Gate 3 requires auth.scripe.org DNS and Vercel domain attachment (EnableCentralNativeAndPasskeyMigration=false, RpId=admin.scripe.org). Gate 4 covers live external IdP credentials plus carried post-launch notes (V10.2.2, IdEncryption fallback, OTP digits/TTL, and FileGuard cell-level FLS).
